title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): X and Y are smooth projective varieties over an algebraically closed field k, and Z is an algebraic correspondence (a cycle on X×Y). A_X = Alb(X) and A_Y = Alb(Y). φ_X : X → A^1_X = X' is the canonical (Albanese) morphism. B = B_X = Pic^0_{A_X/k} is the dual abelian variety, which is canonically Pic^{00}_{X/k}. Θ is the Poincaré class on B×X'.

Construction:
1. Push Z forward to Z' on X'×Y and form Z'' = B×Z' on B×X'×Y.
2. Let π : B×X'×Y → B×Y be the projection. Then c = π_*(z''·Θ) is a numerical class of divisors on B×Y.
3. This page interprets c as a class c' of divisorial correspondences between B and Y. Such a class is the same as a homomorphism A_Y → Pic^0_{B/k}, up to a canonical isomorphism.
4. Cartier biduality, Pic^0_{B/k} = A_X^{**} ≅ A_X, then yields a homomorphism of abelian varieties u_Z : A_Y → A_X.
5. u_Z depends only on the numerical class of Z. This is legitimate because Hom(A_Y, A_X) is torsion-free, so numerical and algebraic equivalence of divisorial correspondences agree there.

What it serves:
- Theorem 1.1 asserts that a numerical class of correspondences induces a homomorphism of Albanese varieties compatible with the Albanese summation maps S. Corollary 1.3 says u_Z is that homomorphism: S_X(^tZ(n)) = u_Z(S_Y(n)) for 0-cycles n of degree 0 on Y.
- This is reduced to Lemma 1.4: θ(S_X(Z(n))) = c'(n) in Pic^0 of B. Here θ : A_X(k) → Pic^0(B) is the biduality map.
- On the next page, Lemma 1.4 is in turn reduced to a moving lemma for a divisor D in the class of Θ (Lemma 1.5).

Overall this is the classical functoriality of the Albanese (and Picard) variety with respect to correspondences modulo numerical equivalence. It is part of Grothendieck's preliminaries on how correspondence classes act on H^1-type invariants (Albanese/Picard), in the context of the standard conjectures and motives.
errors: Lemma 1.4 places θ(S_X(Z(n))) in Pic^0(A_X); it should be Pic^0(B), with B = Pic^0_{A_X}, since θ comes from biduality A_X(k) → Pic^0(B). The next page indeed writes Pic^0(B).
Lemma 1.4 writes Z(n); for a 0-cycle n on Y pushed to X it should be the transpose ^tZ(n), as on the next page.
'diviseur de degré 0 sur Y' should read 0-cycle of degree 0 for the Albanese statement (loose wording).

The passage from the numerical class c to a well-defined homomorphism tacitly uses that divisorial correspondences modulo numerical equivalence inject into Hom(A_Y, Pic^0_B), which is torsion-free. This is fine but not stated.

ideas.what: Homomorphism of Albanese varieties induced by an algebraic correspondence, constructed via a divisorial correspondence on (dual Albanese)×Y and Cartier biduality
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of Albanese/Picard varieties under correspondences; action of correspondences on h^1 of motives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (Variétés abéliennes et courbes algébriques, 1948); Lang, Abelian Varieties (1959); Matsusaka
ideas.where_published: Related material in Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968) and Grothendieck's motive notes as reported by Kleiman/Manin; Picard scheme facts in FGA (Exp. 236)

ideas.what: Correspondence classes modulo numerical equivalence suffice to define the homomorphism u_Z
ideas.modern_name: Divisorial correspondences and Hom(A_Y, A_X) being torsion-free; numerical motives h^1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil, Lang; Kleiman (1968) in the motive context

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but classical construction of the Albanese map induced by a correspondence (Weil/Lang theory), reorganized via dual-abelian-variety biduality. It has no new content relative to the literature.
transcription_corrections: The insertion '(à un iso can.' likely reads '(à un iso can. près)', closing with ')' after 'on a'.
'Cl(B×[-A_?-]Y)': the struck-out symbol is an A with an illegible subscript, crossed out; the intended object is Cl(B×Y).
'décalant[?]' is an illegible struck word, possibly 'Décalant' or similar; it is irrelevant to the mathematics.
'Corollaire 1.3' text: '...satisfait à la condition envisagée dans le th. 1.1.' — the earlier sentence says 'le th. 1 résultera', consistent with this.
